candidate: Claude Code built-in Bash sandbox (docs at v2.1.322)
what: OS-level sandbox for the agent's shell commands: Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap plus a proxy on Linux and WSL2, nothing on native Windows
problem_here: Limits what an unattended agent's shell commands can read, write and reach when nobody answers prompts
mechanism: Namespaces confine writes to the working directory; a proxy enforces a domain allow-list; optional read denies and credential masking (sandbox.credentials); failIfUnavailable and allowUnsandboxedCommands=false make it strict
evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments (vendor docs, 2026-11-10): the vendor states the Bash sandbox alone is not sufficient for fully unattended runs. No independent measurement found
maturity: Built in; docs current at v2.1.322 (2026-11); proprietary CLI; escape and fail-open fixes in 2.1.309 to 2.1.321; open user reports of fail-open after a bridge timeout
cost: System packages bubblewrap and socat; AppArmor profile may be needed on Ubuntu; shell only; hides GPU devices and kills detached children, so the run launcher must be excluded; inherits environment secrets unless configured
simpler_alternative: Permission allow-list plus guard hook only (advice level)
